policy: Component-boundary traceability for the shell, sidebar, Header, Settings and right workbench (PARITY_TODO.md §0.1). A group records which Rust files own the behaviour of its Web sources. `ported` requires verifiable evidence (an existing Rust test function or a file under artifacts/); `partial` must name what remains; `excluded` must give a reason. Unlisted sources are reported as pending. The Agent conversation layer is tracked separately in tools/agent-migration-map.json.

excluded_patterns.reason: Browser visual-smoke harness; native verification uses capture modes and Rust tests.
Browser visual-smoke harness; native verification uses capture modes and Rust tests.
Styles or fixtures used only by browser visual-smoke harnesses.
Module barrel; re-exports only. Rust modules use mod.rs/pub use.

groups.name: Style tokens and theme packs
groups.remaining: The five built-in packs and the tokens.css semantic layer are projected into Theme. Installing or removing external sub-theme packages (useSubThemeCatalog / SubThemeStyleHost) and forced-colours mode are not ported.

groups.name: Typography scale and roles
groups.remaining: TYPOGRAPHY_SCALE_METRICS and the UI role sizes follow the three scales. The font catalog (five built-in entries, role resolution with product fallbacks, id normalisation), the locales.css script stacks and their GPUI projection (the first installed family plus a cascade of the installed rest, as Chromium walks font-family) are native: the interface is Geist, code Geist Mono, the terminal the Terminal Mono stack (SF Mono where installed, else Menlo), each over the content language's CJK faces. Not ported: reading the stored puppyone.desktop.typography value with its legacy migrations (part of the Electron preference import, PL-3) and Sub Theme content fonts (S-14).

groups.name: Appearance preferences and runtime
groups.remaining: Theme mode (including following the OS), theme pack, text scale, file icon theme and pointer cursors apply natively. Palette overrides and interface styles are stored but not applied. A first launch imports the Electron product's preferences (PL-3): recent Projects with the last active first, the locale, the appearance v6 document or its legacy keys (colour mode, Sub Theme, typography, pointer cursors, file icons, loading style), pane widths, experiments, files visibility, local agents, Git layout, titlebar actions and first-run sign-in; editor tab layouts and credentials are not imported (the apps keep separate data and Keychain).

groups.name: Interface styles (skins)
groups.reason: Out of scope for this round (PARITY_TODO.md §5): the native shell renders the default interface only and the Appearance page shows the interface-style row disabled.

groups.name: Localization runtime
groups.remaining: Catalogs are bundled rather than lazily loaded. The ICU subset covers what the catalogs use ({arg}, number, plural with =N and #); select and date/relative-time formats are not implemented.

groups.name: Settings composition and controls
groups.remaining: Dialog, sidebar and rows follow settings.css geometry; checked by capture screenshots only. There is no automated pixel comparison against the Web Settings pages.

groups.name: Preferences store
groups.remaining: One persisted owner with serde defaults and legacy migration. Fields whose Web consumer has no native counterpart (share slice, editor presentation details) are not represented.

groups.name: General settings page
groups.remaining: Language and version rows are native. Update download/install needs the Electron updater; the row reports availability only.

groups.name: Appearance settings page
groups.remaining: Theme mode cards, theme pack, file icons, Git layout, loading animation, Header elements and pointer cursors are live. Theme-pack folder/add actions, palette overrides and interface styles are shown disabled (no native theme directory service).

groups.name: Typography settings page
groups.remaining: Scale segment and three-pane preview are ported; the preview renders with bundled fonts rather than the catalog font stacks.

groups.name: Create New settings page and entry registry
groups.remaining: Menu and settings share one registry. Folder, Markdown, text, JSON, CSV and HTML are created natively; specialised formats (documents, slides, apps) are listed but unavailable.

groups.name: Experimental settings page
groups.remaining: Same groups and rows as the Web; rows without a native consumer are shown disabled.

groups.name: Project, Git and Git Ignore settings pages
groups.remaining: Project info, repository facts (branch, upstream, sync, remotes) and Git Ignore (hidden files + exclude patterns applied to the tree) are native. Auto-commit and the workspace backup/source-service config (PuppyoneWorkspaceConfigSettings) are not ported.

groups.name: Other App Imports settings page
groups.remaining: Page structure and visibility gate are ported; import actions need the Electron import services and are shown unavailable.

groups.name: Privacy settings page
groups.remaining: There is no native telemetry service; the analytics row is shown disabled.

groups.name: Account and plan settings pages
groups.remaining: Signed-out states only. Sign-in, credits, plans and seats need cloud services (PARITY_TODO.md §5).

groups.name: Local Agents settings and inventory
groups.remaining: Detected agents with persisted show/hide, rescan, empty/error states and history discovery are native; the Launcher honours hidden agents. The Hooks and setup-guide sections depend on Electron installation/activity services and are hidden, as the Web does when those services are unsupported.

groups.name: Model Connections settings
groups.remaining: List, add/edit and detail flow with Keychain credentials. Local service discovery, tool-support verification and managed (cloud) connections are not ported.

groups.name: Header and window chrome
groups.remaining: Project button, Agent entry (bubble icon with show/hide tooltip), Changes status icons and Header elements are native. Header coachmarks, Reach/Share and cloud location states are not ported.

groups.name: Project menu, location switcher and project rail
groups.remaining: Recent-project list, open folder, Home and remove-from-recents are native; the rail lists recent projects. Per-project row actions (rename/unlink, ProjectRowActions) and cloud locations are not ported.

groups.name: Home page
groups.remaining: Brand lockup, recent projects (sorted by last change, with folder, time and unlink), New empty project with its create dialog, Open a folder and Sign in are native. Import (Git clone, cloud sources) and template links are shown disabled; the onboarding telemetry disclosure is not ported.

groups.name: Explorer tree and file actions
groups.remaining: Local resource mutations now drain and rebind retained Working Copies; Explorer sessions retain trees, selection, scroll and clipboard across projects and revalidate loaded folders. Extension-changing viewer transitions, concurrent scoped mutation queues, directory subscriptions, reference drag into Agent, cross-app drag export and multi-root composition remain incomplete; strict visual and OS drag parity are unverified.

groups.name: Sidebar footer navigation and help
groups.remaining: Settings and Help (product FeedbackHelpIcon) are native in the footer with the product geometry, utility colour, no divider and the tree edge fade; like the product, Git is not in the footer (Changes lives in the Header). Plugins, the rail/top navigation variants and the Project Rail utilities are not ported; the busy pulse grid is a native stand-in for FloatingNoticeStack.

groups.name: Workbench launcher
groups.remaining: Detected agents, the Built-in Agent + Terminal group, rescan, History and discovery status are native and respect hidden agents; Codex uses the monochrome ChatGPT mark like AgentMonochromeBrandImage. Install guides and per-agent activation are not ported.

groups.name: Workbench tabs, split layout and close flow
groups.remaining: 38px tab bar with compact/overflow modes, brand icons with the running-chat dot (AuxiliaryWorkbenchStatus), tab context menu, drag split and close confirmation are native. Session-header motion, tab-move preview animation and render-failure boundaries are not ported.

groups.name: Changes panel (source control)
groups.remaining: Collapsible Staged/Unstaged/Merge/Committed panels with Commit and Stage and Commit (product default message), Pull notice and Push are native and localized. A selected change opens WorkingFileDetail in place (Open file / Stage / Unstage / Discard) over the Diff Registry: the unified text diff (numbered lines, hunk separators, wrapping) and the binary summary (format, before/after sizes, open current file), framed by GitFileDiffSurface. History is the day-grouped timeline with change totals and a four-file preview; a commit opens its summary (HEAD, copyable id, totals) and file diffs. As in the Web (git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree), a folder anywhere inside a work tree is managed and lists the whole repository with repository-relative paths; staging, discarding, diffs and Open file act only on changes inside the opened folder (the Web passes repository paths as folder-relative pathspecs, which fails from a subfolder). Pull/Push/Discard confirm inline rather than in the product's dialogs; the DOCX redline, remote management, incoming-change review and repository setup are not ported.

groups.name: Terminal surface
groups.remaining: Terminal colours come from the pack. The font is the product's Terminal Mono stack; cells follow xterm's WebGL renderer (the W advance floored to device pixels; Blink's whole-pixel font box, x1.24, floored; glyphs on the cell grid on device pixels), with the session padding (14/0/16/16), FitAddon's fit, 6000 lines of scrollback, weight 450/700, the blinking block cursor, the unfocused outline and xterm's cursor initialisation, box drawing/blocks/shades/Powerline from the product's xterm definitions (tools/import-xterm-glyphs.mjs), the hovered link's underline and click activation, the default-style scrollbar (12px lane, 8px thumb while hovered or 900 ms after a scroll), grey system lines for exits and launch failures and the top notice stack. Pixel suite `terminal`: 95.3% with identical geometry; xterm's canvas rasterises glyphs with macOS font smoothing, GPUI without. Not ported: the classic-interface scrollbar (P3 interface styles), xterm checkpoint restore and Unicode 11 width tables (vt100 uses unicode-width).

groups.name: Shared overlays, dialogs and tooltips
groups.remaining: Dialogs and tooltips use GPUI Kit with product tokens. The product scrollbar (scrollbars.css with ScrollbarActivity) is Kit's base scrollbar over each scroll owner: a 12px lane, the thumb transparent at rest and 8px / 2px inset while the owner is hovered (vendor patch) or for 900 ms after it scrolls, the hover colour over the thumb; Settings, Homepage, Explorer, Source Control, History, Agent transcript/history/picker/dock, launcher, menus, dialogs and the PDF/database viewers carry it. The classic-interface arrow buttons belong to the P3 interface styles; the light backdrop composites darker than Chromium (Settings light 86%, under investigation).

groups.name: Markdown viewer (native editor)
groups.remaining: Native live preview and source mode: headings, emphasis, links and wiki links, lists, tasks, quotes, rules, highlighted code blocks and editable tables (PARITY_TODO §7). Not native: KaTeX math, Mermaid, images, HTML and MDX blocks, markdownEnvironment (workspace link graph, wiki-link commands, asset resolver), AI edit review, document navigation, block drag, heading outline, table column resize and viewport virtualisation. The WebView island that ran the product viewer was removed.

groups.name: Text, JSON and code viewers and shared editor infrastructure
groups.remaining: Text, JSON and code files open in the native plain-text editor (find, pane menu, undo, IME). No syntax highlighting, folding, JSON validation or language services outside Markdown code blocks.

groups.name: CSV table viewer
groups.remaining: Native table, source mode, structure operations, column widths, references and find (PARITY_TODO N9). Workspace reference resolution through the product link graph is not ported.

groups.name: HTML viewer (Interact, Edit, Source)
groups.remaining: Interact runs the page in the system WebView; Edit runs the product's HtmlVisualSurface (source index, edit compiler, projection, frame bridge, toolbar, block rail, text input) bundled from the product into the WebView, with the native code editor owning text, history and saves; Source is the native code editor. Not pixel-compared; the Edit page's toolbar uses the bundled Geist Sans and the active Sub Theme tokens. Cloud documents cannot import images (no provider write); the standalone options menu (HtmlViewMenu) is the pane menu instead.

groups.name: Viewer registry
groups.remaining: Markdown and CSV / TSV open in their native editors, other text files in the native code editor; HTML, PDF, image, audio/video, Office and database documents open in their viewers. Context-map, app and PuppyFlow viewers have no native implementation.

groups.name: Editor pane chrome and actions menu
groups.remaining: Native ⋯ handle, actions menu (live / source, CSV view items, find, open externally, close) and find bar for the single pane; multi-pane runtime is tracked under the editor workbench group.

groups.name: Editor document session
groups.remaining: Rust owns the save queue, disk epochs and drains; the native document editor reports dirty state, snapshots and saved receipts over the host protocol, one document per window. The multi-document working-copy registry and external-conflict notices are not ported.

groups.name: Editor workbench: splits, tabs, pane move and file drop
groups.remaining: Local tabs/MRU, recursive panes, retained documents/projects and layout persistence run in the real Shell. Same-workspace single-file Explorer drops focus existing views, fill empty panes or split at an edge, with a preview and target-lifetime fencing. Cloud navigation/drafts, full pane view state, cross-root/native external-drop authority, complete keyboard/accessibility and strict pixel parity remain incomplete.

groups.name: Editor and shared-ui stylesheets (product tokens in native styles)
groups.remaining: Token values are imported from the product CSS (tools/import-editor-theme.mjs → assets/editor); the rules are re-expressed per element in Rust styles. Floating notices, overflow dots and the shared-ui patterns have no native consumer yet.

groups.name: Cloud Homepage catalog and opening choices
groups.remaining: One flat Homepage/Header list, trusted-locator merge, location icons, the Open menu and the per-account opening history are native. The linked badge has no silhouette backplate; the card layout (asset library home) is not ported; no pixel comparison against the TS Homepage with Cloud rows yet.

groups.name: Cloud repository association and Header switch
groups.remaining: MissingCloudProjectRecovery (404 replace-connection flow), the value page and publish hand-off, and pixel comparison of the switch dialog are not ported.

groups.name: Cloud explicit opening and failures
groups.remaining: Concurrent-open coalescing, the recovery dialog's Details disclosure and pixel comparison of the loading and recovery states remain.

groups.name: Cloud live file provider
groups.remaining: Scope targets, copy/import, viewer preview resources (Office/database temp files, HTML data-URL projection) and real-backend acceptance are not covered.

groups.name: Cloud History
groups.remaining: The history graph (HistoryGraphVisual, cloudTopology) and the services-page two-pane History view are not ported.

groups.name: Cloud file workspace
groups.remaining: The hosted shell reuses the native Explorer, editor and viewers; authority changes revoke the selection, reopening rebinds retained Working Copies, and a failed subscription shows the workspace notice with Retry. Cloud preview resources (Office/database temp files, HTML data-URL projection), Scope targets and real-backend acceptance remain; the floating notices are not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Cloud first publication
groups.remaining: The coordinator (journal v2 with v1 migration, idempotent creation, keychain secret, URL-scoped secure helper, immutable push with lease, remote-truth reconciliation, explicit cleanup) and the activation / running / resume pictures are native. The push receipt endpoint (readInitialPushReceipt) is not consulted (ls-remote only); the transfer meter, the hero artwork and pixel comparison are not ported; acceptance against a real Cloud Git host is pending.

groups.name: Terminal legacy session hosts (unreachable)
groups.reason: Not reachable from the product entry at v0.4.0 (import walk from every non-test, non-harness module): the terminal-owned session header, overflow, tab moves, split groups and session hosts survive only for the visual-smoke harnesses. Production terminals are Auxiliary Workbench items (TerminalWorkbenchContribution), so their tabs, overflow, moves and splits are the shared workbench ones (src/features/workbench).

groups.name: Terminal workbench item
groups.note: Terminal items are titled by the project folder with the launcher as their icon; the overflow detail is 'folder — status'; a starting or running session confirms before closing; 32 terminals per project; sessions live per project and survive project switches; the PTY bridge, its control queue and process budget are platform::terminal. The terminal feature gate is the header's terminal preference. Of terminalSessions.ts production uses only the session types (its reducer serves the unreachable legacy hosts).
